messages.subject: problems with datetime x-axis
parts:
Hello,

I am having some problems with inconsistency in ggplot successfully
generating a stacked time series plot. I've done quite a bit of
searching and this does not appear to be a new issue, but none of the
work-arounds have been successful. In addition, this code was working
fine previously, and I'm not sure what changed to cause the problem.
Windows 7 64 bit, R 2.14.2, ggplot2 0.9

This is the error message:
Error in seq.int(0, to0 - from, by) : 'to' must be finite

code:
well.data = read.csv("hobo_pres_temp_stacked_truncated.csv", head =
TRUE)
date.time = as.POSIXct(well.data$date_time, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M:
%S", "America/Los_Angeles")
n = length(well.data$temp)

temperature = (well.data$temp[seq(1,n,4)] - 32)*(5/9) # note
conversion to C
dateTime = as.POSIXct((as.numeric(date.time[seq(1,n,4)])%/%3600*3600)
, origin = "1970-01-01"
,tz = "America/Los_Angeles")
loggerID = well.data$logger_id[seq(1,n,4)]
date.temp.data = data.frame(loggerID, dateTime, temperature)

ggplot(date.temp.data, aes(dateTime, temperature)) +
geom_line() + facet_grid(loggerID~.)

trying it this way:
ggplot(date.temp.data, aes(dateTime, temperature)) +
geom_line() + facet_grid(loggerID~.) +
scale_x_datetime(major = "month")

produced this error:
Error in continuous_scale(aesthetics, "datetime", identity, breaks =
breaks, :
unused argument(s) (major = "month")

Thanks, B

messages.author: 3db8f66cdf0eadb4
messages.subject: Re: problems with datetime x-axis
parts:
I answered my own question. The culprit: Excel. I manipulated the
text file for the data and Excel messed up the datetime format, I
should know better. as.POSIXct did not bark a warning and produced an
object of NAs. Since the code was working previously, I did not
immediately check the workspace. The code works now.
